concepts.learning_objective: Express a fraction or decimal as a percentage by finding an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 or multiplying by 100.
Express a percentage z% as the fraction z/100 and its equivalent forms.
Explain why expressing quantities as parts per hundred makes comparison of proportions easier.
Find a given percentage of a quantity using fraction, decimal or proportional reasoning.
Compute percentages mentally by combining easy percentages such as 10%, 5% and 20%.
Convert a ratio of parts into a fraction of the whole and then into a percentage.

topics.title: Finding the Whole and Percentages Greater than 100

concepts.learning_objective: Find the whole quantity or the remaining part when a percentage of it is known.
Interpret percentages greater than 100 as more than the whole and relate them to decimals and multiples.
Use percentages to compare proportions when the wholes are different.
Calculate percentage increase or decrease with respect to the original amount.
Calculate profit or loss percentage with respect to the cost price, and find cost or selling price from it.
Find the selling price after a percentage discount on the marked price.
Find the final price of an item when a tax such as GST is added as a percentage.
Find the amount after t years without compounding using p(1 + rt).
Find the amount after t years with compounding using p(1 + r)^t.
Find the value of a quantity that decreases by a fixed percentage over one or more periods.
Recognise that successive percentage changes compound and do not simply add.
Distinguish between comparing percentages and comparing absolute amounts.
